items.summary: AIHOT is an open-source platform that allows users to customize their own industry-specific hot topic websites. It supports multiple data sources including RSS feeds, web lists, JSON interfaces, X accounts, and custom scripts. Users can input their own industry-specific criteria and standards by modifying the `industry/` folder contents, including `sources.json` for data sources and `prompts/` for industry-specific knowledge. The platform features automated clustering, daily report generation, and a user-friendly interface. The creator has made the core components, including the data collection, selection, and clustering mechanisms, publicly available to encourage adaptation for various industries. However, specific data sources and some proprietary strategies are not disclosed to maintain exclusivity and avoid potential disputes.

items.title: coucou
items.description: A tiny friend that lives in your notch (macOS) or at the top of your screen (Windows, Linux) and keeps an eye on your coding agents: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity and more.
items.summary: The sources mention several AI coding agent apps that live in the notch or at the top of the screen: Vibe Island supports multiple AI coding agents including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and more, offering interaction features like permission requests and Markdown rendering. CodeIsland is a free, open-source macOS app that turns the notch into a dashboard for AI coding agents, showing session lists and usage stats. Codenotch is a macOS app that pins usage limits from various coding agents to a screen edge, unfolding when the pointer reaches it. Buddi is an animated pet that reacts to what Claude Code is doing, offering personality over a plain status bar. The sources do not provide a definitive answer on which app is the best for all users.

items.title: dots
items.description: Open-source dots for the web: an AI agent with its own browser, one that does not get blocked.
items.summary: The sources describe "dots" as an open-source AI agent with its own browser designed to avoid being blocked. It is associated with GitHub and has over 1,900 stars. The browser is built around a real Firefox engine patched in C++ to ensure it cannot be detected as an automation tool. It is not affiliated with OpenAI and is MIT licensed. The browser provides a consistent identity per seed, ensuring that screen, fonts, GPU, timezone, and language agree with each other, and it does not reveal any signs of automation to web pages.

items.title: jevgrep
items.description: Find code by asking what it does. A CLI for coding agents that uses Jev to discover relevant files and source context.
items.summary: Jevgrep is a command line tool for coding agents that uses Jev to discover relevant files and source context by asking what the code does. It reduces the cost of coding agents by providing relevant files, search leads, and source excerpts in one response, thus minimizing the time spent on searching unfamiliar repositories. It can be installed via npm with the command `npm install -g @ddeng/jevgrep`. The tool is designed to help coding agents move directly toward implementation and testing by providing necessary context upfront.

items.summary: The sources describe a comprehensive logo-design skill for AI agents like Claude, Gemini CLI, and Codex, which includes principles, process, SVG craft, testing tools, and a 1,400+ logo reference library. items.title: onetake
items.description: Motion films that never cut to the next slide: every beat grows out of the one before, one continuous camera, continuity measured by an oracle. A Claude Agent Skill for product launch films and feature demos.
items.summary: onetake is a motion film technology that creates continuous-camera demo videos without cuts between scenes, ensuring each beat grows out of the previous one. It uses a Claude Agent Skill to generate 15- to 30-second product launch films, teasers, and feature demos. The technology employs an oracle script to measure transition continuity and rejects films below a threshold before human review. The continuous virtual camera follows transformations without cutting, anticipating where elements will land and reacting to impacts, maintaining strict visual continuity and camera motion consistency.

items.title: yomiyasu
items.description: AI生成の日本語を自然な日本語へ推敲するAgent Skill / Agent Skill for Refining AI-Generated Japanese into Natural Japanese
items.summary: The sources describe an AI-generated Japanese refinement agent skill called "yomiyasu" that aims to convert AI-generated unnatural Japanese into more natural and readable text. The skill targets various aspects of text structure and style, such as nested negations, long and redundant expressions, and overly complex sentence structures. While some users find the skill useful for improving readability, others criticize it for not fully addressing the root causes of AI-generated text's unnaturalness, such as cultural and linguistic differences between English and Japanese. The skill's effectiveness and necessity are debated, with some suggesting that human intervention remains crucial for final refinement.

items.title: ten-levels-of-jev
items.description: Ten levels of Jev, from one smart if statement to a coding agent that reaches for Jev on its own
items.summary: The sources describe Jev as TypeSafe's System One model, which reads text only and does not generate text or code. It operates through three question types: Choice, Score, and Noul. Choice selects an option from up to 255, Score rates states against two to ten levels, and Noul answers yes-or-no questions with probability. Jev is used in workflows to verify claims against transcripts and in coding agents to check if tasks are done by answering "is the task done?" before running commands. It classifies commands as read-only, reversible, or irreversible and checks for risky actions. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to the ten-levels-of-Jev concept.
